Senses.Explanation: The broad, long tongue-mark is a Buddha-mark that Chan records transfer to mountains, trees, snow, letters, and responsive speech when these are made to voice the teaching. Dahui Zonggao says that even if all grasses and trees displayed broad, long tongues and spoke until the end of time, they would still deliver only half the canon. Hongzhi Zhengjue instead says wind-blown trees and snowy ground expose the tongue-mark with nowhere to hide it. Feiyin Tongrong gives every manifested body such a tongue to speak, then asks what it says. Nanyuan Daoming answers a request for one word by sticking out his tongue and postponing speech until he has the mark. The image can therefore magnify speech, relocate it into the whole scene, or expose the inadequacy of speech.
